title: Outlook on the web: tenant default for using commas to separate recipients
notes: claim 32: severity major on a rationale: risk rating lowered to minor; ratings are judgements and cannot hold a page
claim 35: severity blocker on a rationale: impact rating lowered to minor; ratings are judgements and cannot hold a page
summary: Hold: the advice to test the cmdlet on a mailbox group is inconsistent with its organisation-wide scope. The briefing also claims that only Outlook on the web users are affected while acknowledging that the new Outlook scope is undocumented. The PowerShell control and roadmap facts are supported, and the previously reported fetch failures did not recur.

claims.where: controls[0].api; summary; What's changing; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Exchange PowerShell documents Set-OrganizationConfig -RecipientDelimiters $false to set the organisation-wide recipient delimiter default.
claims.quote:
The RecipientDelimiters parameter specifies the organization-wide default for the Mail Compose and Reply setting that controls whether commas are used to separate recipients. Valid values are:

- $true: Commas are used to separate recipients by default. This value is the default.

claims.claim: RecipientDelimiters is available only in Exchange Online, the cloud-based service.
claims.quote:
Applicable: Exchange Online

This parameter is available only in the cloud-based service.

claims.claim: Running the cmdlet requires assigned Exchange permissions, and Learn directs readers to the cmdlet-permissions reference.
claims.quote: You need to be assigned permissions before you can run this cmdlet. Although this article lists all parameters for the cmdlet, you might not have access to some parameters if they aren't included in the permissions assigned to you.

claims.claim: The Government Cloud release notes describe the user delimiter setting in the June 13, 2025 entry.
claims.quote:
## June 13, 2025

*Version: 20250606009.12*

- **[GCC] Setting to toggle comma as recipient delimiter:**

claims.claim: Those release notes say Outlook Web and the New Outlook support semicolons or commas as recipient separators by default.
claims.quote: By default, Outlook Web and the New Outlook support separating recipients by using either a semicolon or a comma.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls
claims.claim: The release notes describe a user choice between using commas as separators and allowing commas within contact names.
claims.quote: This new setting allows users to choose if the comma should be used as a recipient separator or instead allowed as part of the contact name.

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: The release notes say the setting helps organisations whose contacts use the Family name, First name format.
claims.quote: This is helpful for organizations where contacts follow the "Family name, First name" format.

claims.claim: The cited release notes describe Government Cloud channels rather than a Worldwide release.
claims.quote: These release notes provide more information about those changes in Government Cloud Channels.

claims.claim: No Exchange admin center path for the tenant recipient delimiter default is documented at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: RecipientDelimiters Exchange admin center tenant comma recipient delimiter policy UI; "RecipientDelimiters". Opened Set-OrganizationConfig and Outlook on the web in Exchange Online; results supplied no admin UI route for this default.

claims.claim: The licensing model is unknown because no licence specific to RecipientDelimiters is published.
claims.quote: Each user who accesses the Exchange Online service must be assigned to a subscription plan, and each user subscription has its own mailbox.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to included. Replace the notes with: 'This is an option inside Exchange Online. Each user accessing Exchange Online must be assigned a subscription plan; Outlook on the web is listed across the service's plans. No licence or meter specific to RecipientDelimiters is documented as of November 2026.' Cite the already-listed Exchange Online service description.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The parameter reference names no licence for RecipientDelimiters, and no licence, meter or charge specific to this setting is published.
claims.quote: Searched: RecipientDelimiters licensing price meter Exchange Online subscription. Opened Set-OrganizationConfig and Exchange Online service description; neither publishes a setting-specific licence, meter or price.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not state whether the tenant default overrides an existing user choice.
claims.quote: Searched: RecipientDelimiters existing user choice override new Outlook Windows default comma; "RecipientDelimiters". Opened Set-OrganizationConfig and Government Cloud release notes; neither explains precedence over saved user preferences.

claims.claim: The RecipientDelimiters documentation does not state whether the organisation default also applies in new Outlook for Windows.
claims.quote: Searched: RecipientDelimiters existing user choice override new Outlook Windows default comma; "RecipientDelimiters". Opened Set-OrganizationConfig, Government Cloud release notes and Outlook on the web in Exchange Online; no parameter-specific Windows scope statement found.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The control is admin-opt-in: commas remain separators by default unless an administrator configures the alternative default.
claims.quote:
$true: Commas are used to separate recipients by default. This value is the default.
- $false: Commas aren't used to separate recipients by default.

claims.claim: The PowerShell parameter is the only documented administrative control for this tenant default.
claims.quote: Searched: "RecipientDelimiters"; RecipientDelimiters Exchange admin center tenant comma recipient delimiter policy UI; "recipient" "delimiter" "Set-MailboxMessageConfiguration". Read the parameter reference and search results; no other tenant-default control found.

claims.claim: The cited sources describe no new data access for this setting.
claims.quote: Searched: Outlook recipient delimiter setting comma data access autonomous actions. Opened Set-OrganizationConfig, Government Cloud release notes, Outlook on the web in Exchange Online and Exchange Online service description; none describes new data access for the setting.

claims.claim: The policy reads no new data.
claims.quote: Searched: Outlook recipient delimiter setting comma data access autonomous actions. Opened Set-OrganizationConfig and Government Cloud release notes; they describe the preference but do not state that the policy reads no new data.
claims.fix: Replace 'it reads no new data' with 'the cited sources describe no new data access'.

claims.claim: The setting takes no action on its own and involves no agent or automation.
claims.quote: Searched: Outlook recipient delimiter setting comma data access autonomous actions. Opened Set-OrganizationConfig and Government Cloud release notes; neither makes a statement about autonomous actions, agents or automation.
claims.fix: Replace the bullet with: 'The cited documentation describes a recipient-delimiter preference, not an autonomous action.'

claims.claim: The tenant-default cmdlet can be tested on a pilot mailbox group as an alternative to a pilot tenant.
claims.quote: The RecipientDelimiters parameter specifies the organization-wide default for the Mail Compose and Reply setting that controls whether commas are used to separate recipients.
claims.fix: Replace 'Test the cmdlet on a pilot tenant or mailbox group and read back the result before announcing a change.' with 'Test the cmdlet in a pilot tenant and read back the result before announcing a change.' The documented control sets an organisation-wide default, not a mailbox-group default.

claims.claim: Only users composing or replying in Outlook on the web notice the tenant-default change.
claims.quote: Searched: RecipientDelimiters existing user choice override new Outlook Windows default comma; "RecipientDelimiters". Opened Set-OrganizationConfig and Government Cloud release notes; neither excludes new Outlook from the tenant default's scope.
claims.fix: Replace the impact rationale with: 'Low. This is an administrator-configured recipient-delimiter default. The roadmap lists Web; whether the tenant default also affects new Outlook for Windows is not stated for this parameter.'

controlChecks.governs: Organisation-wide default for whether commas separate recipients in Mail Compose and Reply
